sections.h2: Where is Corvallis, Oregon, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Corvallis is the Benton County seat, on the Willamette River in west-central Oregon at an elevation of 256 feet. The city covers roughly 14.5 square miles, and Interstate 5 is 10 to 12 miles to the east.

Eugene is 44 miles south, Portland is 85 miles north, and the northwest edge of town meets the foothills of the Coast Range, where Bald Hill overlooks the city. Corvallis is the westernmost city in the contiguous states with more than 50,000 residents.

The 2020 census counted 59,922 people, and the 2023 estimate was 61,087. The median age is 27.5.

sections.h2: What is the history of Corvallis?
sections.html:
Joseph Avery built the first home within today's city limits in 1845 or 1846 and platted a supply town called Marysville in 1849. The Territorial Legislature renamed it Corvallis in 1853, and the city was incorporated on January 29, 1857.

A faction briefly made Corvallis the territorial capital in 1855 before the capital returned to Salem. Land donated in 1851 for the county seat is where the Benton County Courthouse stands today.

sections.h2: How do Oregon State University and other employers shape the Corvallis housing market?
sections.html:
Oregon State University is the dominant employer and driver of housing demand in Corvallis. Its 420-acre main campus enrolls about 24,900 students, and more than 5,250 of them live in 16 residence halls.

Corvallis runs two water treatment plants with capacity of about 19 million gallons a day, drawing on the Rock Creek watershed and the Willamette River. The city has four fire stations, at least 47 parks, and the Tree City USA designation.

The Corvallis metro economy produced $6.035 billion in GDP in 2023, and the city is part of the Silicon Forest technology corridor. Benton County ties its economy to the university, agriculture, lumber and printing technology research.

sections.h2: Who owns and who rents in Corvallis?
sections.html:
Corvallis is mostly a renter city: 59.9 percent of occupied homes are rented and 40.1 percent are owner-occupied. The 2020 census counted 25,732 housing units, 7.2 percent of them vacant.

  • Homeowner vacancy rate: 1.2 percent
  • Rental vacancy rate: 7.2 percent
  • Households: 23,876, with 33.3 percent living alone

Those numbers shape a sale. A small owner-occupied market means houses for sale compete with a large pool of rentals, and many sellers are landlords. If you own a rental here, the tenant rules below matter before any buyer walks through.

sections.h2: What tenant rules apply when I sell a Corvallis rental?
sections.html:
Oregon's ORS 90.427 controls how a landlord can end a tenancy for a sale. After the tenant's first year, a landlord needs an accepted offer from a buyer who will live in the home and must give at least 90 days of written notice, delivered within 120 days of accepting the offer.

The landlord pays one month's rent when delivering the notice, except landlords with four or fewer covered units. During the first year, a month-to-month tenancy can end without cause on 30 days' notice. Violations can cost three months' rent plus damages, and the tenant has up to a year to bring the claim.

Fixed-term leases generally cannot be ended mid-term on the sale ground, so a fixed-term tenancy usually stays with the house until it expires. Buyers who purchase with the tenant in place avoid the notice rules altogether.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Corvallis and what does it do to houses?
sections.html:
Corvallis has a warm-summer Mediterranean climate, with warm dry summers and mild wet winters. Annual precipitation is about 43 inches at Oregon State University and up to 66 inches in the northwest hills. Snow is rare, averaging 2.9 inches a year, and seldom lasts more than a day.

Midwinter fog can cut visibility to about 20 feet. The record high is 110 degrees and the record low is minus 8.

  • Roof and gutter condition matter after a wet winter
  • The northwest hills get the most rain, up to 66 inches a year
  • Water runs through the city in the Willamette, Mary's River and 13 creeks, so check a house's flood status

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and schools are in Corvallis?
sections.html:
Corvallis neighborhoods include Glenridge and Timberhill in the northwest, Cardwell Hill and Bald Hill to the southwest, Crystal Lake in the south, Village Green, Conifer and Crescent Valley in the northeast, and Eastgate and Peoria in the east. The College Hill West Historic District sits near the university.

The Corvallis School District runs two high schools, Corvallis High School and Crescent Valley High School, and both draw students from parts of the city. Linn-Benton Community College has a Benton Center campus here.

sections.h2: How do people get around Corvallis?
sections.html:
Oregon 34 links Corvallis to I-5 and to Philomath, US 20 leads to Albany, and Oregon 99W runs to Eugene and McMinnville. Corvallis Transit System runs nine routes and has been fareless since 2011.

Biking is unusually common. A 2009 figure put bicycle commuting at 9.3 percent, the highest of any U.S. metro area, and a 2013 count had 72.6 percent driving alone and 7.7 percent working from home. Commercial flights leave from Eugene, 35 miles away, and Amtrak Cascades stops at the Albany station.

sections.h2: What else should I know about Benton County?
sections.html:
Benton County is small, covering 679 square miles, which makes it the fourth-smallest Oregon county by land area. It borders Polk County to the north, Lincoln County to the west, Linn County to the east and Lane County to the south.

Besides Corvallis, the county includes Adair Village, Monroe, Philomath and the part of Albany north of downtown. Its 2025 population estimate is 97,728, so Corvallis holds well over half of the county's residents.

sections.h2: How do Benton County property taxes work if I sell in Corvallis?
sections.html:
Benton County property taxes are due November 15, with a 3 percent discount for full payment and installments in thirds. The county's 2024 notice listed November 15, February 15 and May 15, and late interest under ORS 311.505 starts after that, accruing from December 16 on a late first installment.

At closing, escrow splits the year's bill between you and the buyer, so ask the escrow officer for the proration figure.

faqs.a: Corvallis is in Benton County and is its county seat. Benton County had 95,184 residents in the 2020 census.

faqs.q: When are Corvallis property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15 is the due date, and paying in full by then earns a 3 percent discount. Thirds are due November 15, February 15 and May 15.
Yes. About 59.9 percent of occupied housing is renter-occupied, compared with 40.1 percent owner-occupied.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Corvallis rental while the tenant lives there?
faqs.a: Yes. Many owners sell with the tenant in place. If you need the tenant out for an owner-occupant buyer, ORS 90.427 requires 90 days of written notice and a payment of one month's rent in most cases.

faqs.q: Does Corvallis get snow or flooding?
faqs.a: Snow is rare at about 2.9 inches a year. Our sources give no flood-zone data, so check FEMA maps for your address.
